docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
SeaTicket is a ticketing system and AI agent that support your community.

It lets you consolidate all your software issues from GitHub, forums, emails, and more into a single intelligent platform. Enable AI agents to assist your team in autonomously resolving problems.

docs.title: First team administrator
docs.text: The standard Docker deployment creates the first team administrator from INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL and INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD on first startup. Use this account for normal SeaTicket work and team administration.

docs.title: Add a system administrator
docs.text:
Ensure the container is running, then enter this command:

docker exec -it seaqa-web /scripts/reset-admin.sh

Enter the email address and password according to the prompts. This creates a system administrator, not a team administrator.

System administrators do not belong to a team and can only access the system administration interface. Most deployments do not need one for daily use.

docs.title: Forgot a system administrator password?
docs.text: Create a new system administrator as described above, then use it to reset the password for the old system administrator account.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
Use the following command to clear expired session records in sea_qa database:

cd seaqa-web
python3 manage.py clearsessions

Tip

Enter into the docker image, then go to /opt/seaticket/seaqa-web

docs.title: SeaTicket Indexer periodic cleanup
docs.text: SeaTicket Indexer runs periodic cleanup tasks (default: every 24 hours). The tasks remove records in the following databases.

docs.title: SeaTicket database (project connection metadata)
docs.text:
• Deleted connections in project_connection
  • Deleted projects in deleted_projects (after cleanup, related connections for the project are removed)

docs.title: SeaDB (connection data tables)
docs.text:
• For recently updated connections (default: updated within the last 7 days)
  • Delete rows that are marked deleted=true and have been deleted for more than 14 days
  • For deleted connections
  • Drop the SeaDB tables that belong to the connection

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
Use the following command to clean the login records:

use sea_qa;
DELETE FROM sysadmin_extra_userloginlog WHERE to_days(now()) - to_days(login_date) > 90;

docs.title: Clean chat sessions
docs.text:
SeaTicket Web provides a management command to clean old chat data in batches. By default, it keeps the last 90 days.

Tip

Enter into the docker image, then go to /opt/seaticket/seaqa-web

python3 manage.py clean_chat_sessions

You can change the retention period by passing --days:

python3 manage.py clean_chat_sessions --days=90

This command deletes:

  • chat_sessions older than the cutoff date
  • chat_messages linked to expired sessions
  • chat_message_thought_process linked to expired sessions
  • Orphaned chat_messages and chat_message_thought_process rows with no corresponding session

docs.title: Clean notifications
docs.text:
SeaTicket Events runs a periodic notification cleanup task (default: every 24 hours). By default it keeps the last 30 days, and the interval/retention can be configured in NOTIFICATION_CLEANER.

This task deletes old records in batches from:

  • user_notifications
  • project_notification

You can also clean these tables manually as follows.

use sea_qa;
DELETE FROM user_notifications WHERE `timestamp` < '<cutoff_date>';

DELETE FROM project_notification WHERE `timestamp` < '<cutoff_date>';

docs.title: Clean portal external invitations
docs.text:
Portal external invitation tokens that expire after a fixed time window (default: 72 hours). Expired invitations should be cleaned to reduce stale records.

You can also clean these tables manually as follows.

DELETE FROM portal_external_invitations WHERE expire_time < '<cutoff_date>';

docs.title: Clean AI usage statistics
docs.text:
AI usage statistics are stored in ai_usage_statistics and should be cleaned by date. The filter field is date.

You can also clean these tables manually as follows.

DELETE FROM ai_usage_statistics WHERE `date` < '<cutoff_date>';

docs.title: Column Management Guide
docs.text: This guide provides instructions on how to add or delete columns in different table types using the manage_column.sh script.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Before running any commands, navigate to the script directory:

cd /opt/seaticket/seaqa-indexer/seaqa_indexer/script

docs.title: 1. Connection Table Operations
docs.text: Use these commands to manage columns for tables with the connection type (e.g., seafile).

docs.title: Delete a Column
docs.text:
To remove an existing column, use the delete-column action: 

./manage_column.sh delete-column \
    --table-name seafile \
    --table-type connection \
    --column-name test1

docs.title: Add a Column
docs.text:
To add a new column, specify the column name, type, and data mapping: 

./manage_column.sh add-column \
    --table-name seafile \
    --table-type connection \
    --column-name test1 \
    --column-type list \
    --column-data-name list_int

docs.title: 2. Project Table Operations
docs.text: Use these commands to manage columns for tables with the project type (e.g., tickets).

docs.title: Delete a Column
docs.text:
./manage_column.sh delete-column \
    --table-name tickets \
    --table-type project \
    --column-name test1

docs.title: Add a Column
docs.text:
./manage_column.sh add-column \
    --table-name tickets \
    --table-type project \
    --column-name test1 \
    --column-type list \
    --column-data-name list_int

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text:
For detailed information on all available parameters and options, run the help command:

./manage_column.sh -h

docs.title: Parameter Overview:
docs.text:
• --table-name: The name of the target table (e.g., seafile, tickets).
  • --table-type: The category of the table (connection or project).
  • --column-name: The identifier for the column being modified.
  • --column-type: The logical type of the column (e.g., list).
  • --column-data-name: The underlying data structure type (e.g., list_int).

docs.title: Index Management Guide
docs.text: This document provides instructions for rebuilding indices within the SeaQA Indexer system.

docs.title: Rebuilding Indices
docs.text: Rebuilding an index is typically a two-step process: clearing the existing index and then updating it with fresh data.

docs.title: Rebuild Connection Index
docs.text:
Use these commands to rebuild the index for a specific connection.

  1. Navigate to the script directory: 

    cd /opt/seaticket/seaqa-indexer/seaqa_indexer/script

  2. Clear the existing index: 

    ./rebuild_index.sh --connection-id <CONNECTION_ID> clear

  3. Update the index: 

    ./rebuild_index.sh --connection-id <CONNECTION_ID> update

docs.title: Rebuild Project Index
docs.text:
Use these commands to rebuild the index for a specific project.

  1. Navigate to the script directory: 

    cd /opt/seaqa-indexer/seaqa_indexer/index/script

  2. Clear the existing index: 

    ./rebuild_index.sh --project-uuid <PROJECT_UUID> clear

  3. Update the index: 

    ./rebuild_index.sh --project-uuid <PROJECT_UUID> update

Note: Replace <CONNECTION_ID> and <PROJECT_UUID> with your actual connection ID and project UUID respectively.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SeaTicket uses multi-tenancy by default. Every normal user belongs to a team.

The standard Docker deployment automatically creates the first team and a team administrator. Use this account for normal SeaTicket work, including creating projects and managing team members.

The system administrator is an optional maintenance account. It does not belong to any team and cannot use normal SeaTicket features; it can only access the system administration interface. Create one only when you need system-level administration.

docs.title: Cloudflare Turnstile
docs.text:
Cloudflare Turnstile is a privacy-preserving CAPTCHA alternative that helps verify visitors are human. It can be used on the Seafile registration page to reduce automated account creation and protect against registration attacks.

For more information, refer to the Cloudflare Turnstile documentation.

docs.title: .env
docs.text: The .env file will be used to specify the general settings of the components used by the SeaTicket-docker instance and the environment variables required by each component.

docs.title: SeaTicket Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default Value SEATICKET_SERVER_PROTOCOL SeaTicket server protocol (http or https) http SEATICKET_SERVER_HOSTNAME SeaTicket server hostname or domain (required) JWT_PRIVATE_KEY JWT_PRIVATE_KEY, A random string with a length of no less than 32 characters is required for SeaTicket, which can be generated by using pwgen -s 40 1 (required)

docs.title: SeaDB settings
docs.text:
Variable Description Default Value SEADB_SERVER_URL SeaDB server URL. http://seadb:8888 INIT_SEADB_ROOT_PASSWORD Optional separate SeaDB root password. Used only to initialize SeaDB and create its application account. If empty, Compose uses the MySQL initialization root password. INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD SEADB_USERNAME Optional separate SeaDB API username. If empty, Compose uses the MySQL application username. MYSQL_DB_USER (seaticket if unset) SEADB_PASSWORD Optional separate SeaDB API password. If empty, Compose uses the MySQL application password. MYSQL_DB_PASSWORD

By default, SeaDB reuses the MySQL root password for initialization and the MySQL application username/password for API access. Leave all three SeaDB credential variables empty for a standard deployment. Set any of them to use separate credentials; each variable falls back independently.

SeaTicket components authenticate to SeaDB with HTTP Basic authentication. Compose maps the resolved username to SEADB_USER inside the containers. On first deployment, SeaDB runs sea-db init to create root; seaqa-web then uses that root account to register the non-root application account with default_role. JWT_PRIVATE_KEY configures the SeaDB service itself and is not a SeaDB API access token.

After successful initialization, remove both INIT_SEADB_ROOT_PASSWORD and INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD from .env and recreate the containers with docker compose up -d. Keep MySQL application credentials and any separate SeaDB application credentials available on every startup. For existing deployments that used first-team credentials for SeaDB, explicitly set SEADB_USERNAME and SEADB_PASSWORD to those existing values before adopting these defaults. See SeaDB Settings for initialization and default-template SQL commands.

docs.title: SeaSearch Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default Value SEASEARCH_URL Your SeaSearch server API endpoint url, e.g., http://<your seasearch host>:4080 (required) SEASEARCH_TOKEN Your authorization token for accessing SeaSearch API, which can be constructed in echo -n '<your_seasearch_username>:<your_seasearch_password>' | base64 (required)

docs.title: Mysql Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default Value MYSQL_DB_HOST The host of MySQL server. Use db for the bundled MariaDB service. db MYSQL_DB_PORT The port of MySQL server 3306 MYSQL_DB_USER The user for accessing MySQL server seaticket MYSQL_DB_PASSWORD The password of MySQL server (none) MYSQL_DB_NAME The SeaTicket database name seaticket_db INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD Root password for MySQL/MariaDB, bundled or external. Required for the first automatic database, user, and schema initialization. May be removed after successful deployment; subsequent startups use the application account and persistent initialization state. (none) INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_NAME Name of the first SeaTicket team. Used only when no team exists. SeaTicket INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL Email address of the first team administrator. Used only when no team exists. (none) INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD Password of the first team administrator. Used only when no team exists. (none)

docs.title: Redis Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default Value REDIS_HOST The host of Redis server (required) REDIS_PORT The port of Redis server 6379 REDIS_PASSWORD The password of Redis server (none)

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default Value ENABLE_NOTIFICATION_SERVER Enable the WebSocket notification client in seaqa-web false

docs.title: Storage Settings
docs.text:
The Docker deployment defaults to local disk for both attachments and SeaSearch. No S3 service is required with these defaults.

Variable Description Default Value ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND Attachment backend used by the web service, IO service, indexer, and optional portal. Available values: disk, s3. disk SS_STORAGE_TYPE Optional SeaSearch backend override (disk or s3). Unset or empty values fall back to ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND, then disk. Follows ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND SEATICKET_VOLUME Host directory for SeaTicket configuration, logs, and persistent application data. /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data SS_DATA_PATH Host directory for persistent SeaSearch data. /opt/seasearch-data

Local attachment storage

With ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=disk, attachments are saved under ${SEATICKET_VOLUME}/data/attachments on the host (/opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/data/attachments by default), in project_attachments and connection_attachments subdirectories. Back up this directory along with the other persistent application data.

The web and indexer images fix the internal root at /opt/seaticket/data/attachments, with /opt/seaticket/data linked to /shared/data. Do not configure ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_LOCAL_ROOT in .env or seaticket_config.yaml.

Changing storage backends

Existing S3 deployments must set ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 explicitly before using the new deployment defaults. Changing ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND or SS_STORAGE_TYPE does not migrate existing data.

docs.title: Optional S3 Settings
docs.text:
Leave these values empty for a default disk deployment. Configure them only when attachments or SeaSearch use s3. See Use S3 as the storage backend for an example.

Variable Description Required when / Default Value S3_HOST S3-compatible endpoint, e.g., https://s3-endpoint.example.com or https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com. Attachments or SeaSearch use S3 S3_KEY_ID S3 access key ID. Attachments or SeaSearch use S3 S3_SECRET_KEY S3 secret access key. Attachments or SeaSearch use S3 S3_FILE_BUCKET Bucket for uploaded files. ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 S3_WEB_CRAWL_BUCKET Bucket for connection assets, such as email attachments. ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 S3_SEASEARCH_BUCKET Bucket for SeaSearch data. Mapped to S3_SS_BUCKET unless explicitly overridden by that variable. Resolved SS_STORAGE_TYPE=s3 S3_AWS_REGION AWS region for SeaSearch S3 requests. us-east-1 S3_USE_V4_SIGNATURE Use Signature Version 4 for SeaSearch S3 requests. true S3_PATH_STYLE_REQUEST Use path-style S3 requests in SeaSearch. true S3_SSE_C_KEY Optional SeaSearch SSE-C encryption key. Requires HTTPS and Signature Version 4. Empty

The four advanced options above configure SeaSearch. The attachment backend uses Signature Version 4 and path-style requests directly and does not read these options. Create the buckets required by the selected backends and grant the configured credentials read and write access.

docs.title: First Team Settings
docs.text: On a new deployment, SeaTicket automatically creates the first team, its team administrator, and the administrator's initial workspace. This account is a normal SeaTicket user and team administrator, not a system administrator. Existing teams are never changed when the container restarts.

docs.title: SeaSearch Settings
docs.text:
By default, SeaSearch creates its first account from INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL and INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD. Set both INIT_SS_ADMIN_USER and INIT_SS_ADMIN_PASSWORD to use a separate SeaSearch account instead. In either case, set SEASEARCH_TOKEN to the Base64 value of the actual SeaSearch username and password:

echo -n '<username>:<password>' | base64

docs.title: Advanced system systems
docs.text: Variable Description Default Value SEATICKET_LOG_TO_STDOUT Record logs to container standard output false TIME_ZONE Timezone of SeaTicket server UTC

docs.title: seaqa_web_settings.py
docs.text: seaqa_web_settings.py is used to customize the SeaTicket web (seaqa-web) settings.

docs.title: Team role permissions
docs.text:
SeaTicket provides built-in team roles, and each role has a set of permissions. You can customize these permissions with the ENABLED_ROLE_PERMISSIONS setting.

Built-in team roles:

  • free
  • starter
  • pro
  • business
  • enterprise

docs.title: Available permissions
docs.text:
The following options can be configured per team role:

Option Description Default can_add_project Allow users in the role to create projects. True can_add_group Allow users in the role to create groups. True can_use_saml Allow SAML SSO for this role. False for free/starter/pro, True for business/enterprise ai_credit AI credits for the team. Set -1 for unlimited. -1

docs.title: Configuration example
docs.text:
# seaqa_web_settings.py
ENABLED_ROLE_PERMISSIONS = {
    'free': {
        'can_add_project': True,
        'can_add_group': True,
        'can_use_saml': False,
        'ai_credit': -1,
    },
    'starter': {
        'can_use_saml': False,
        'ai_credit': 2000,
    },
    'pro': {
        'ai_credit': 5000,
    },
    'business': {
        'can_use_saml': True,
    },
    'enterprise': {
        'can_use_saml': True,
    },
}

docs.title: Merge behavior
docs.text:
SeaTicket merges your custom settings with the defaults:

  • If you only override part of a role’s permissions, the missing fields inherit from the default settings.
  • If you omit a role entirely, it inherits from free defaults.

For example, the above configuration only changes the keys you specify and keeps the rest consistent with the built-in defaults.

docs.title: Basic settings
docs.text:
General site metadata and links for the login and registration pages. Email settings are documented in Sending Email Notifications.

# Base name used in email sending
SITE_NAME = 'SeaTicket'

# Browser tab's title
SITE_TITLE = 'SeaTicket'

# privacy policy link and service link
PRIVACY_POLICY_LINK = 'https://your-domain/policy'
TERMS_OF_SERVICE_LINK = 'https://your-domain/terms'

# Redirect URL after logout; falls back to the default logout page when empty
LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL = 'https://example.com/<your-own-logout-page>'

# Custom language code choices (overrides defaults in `settings.py` when needed)
LANGUAGES = (
    ('en', 'English'),
    ('zh-cn', '简体中文'),
    ('zh-tw', '繁體中文'),
)

# Force default language for anonymous users (e.g., 'en', 'zh-cn')
FORCE_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = ''

# Path to the background image file of login page(relative to the media path)
LOGIN_BG_IMAGE_PATH = 'img/login-bg.jpg'

docs.title: UI customization
docs.text: Visual branding and UI assets for the web interface. Default assets use LOGO_PATH/FAVICON_PATH values, while CUSTOM_* paths are optional overrides that only take effect when the corresponding files exist.

docs.title: Logo
docs.text:
LOGO_PATH points to the default logo. If you want to replace it, keep the same key but change the path to your own file.

# Default logo path (relative to media root)
LOGO_PATH = 'img/SeaTicket.png'

# Optional logo size override
LOGO_WIDTH = ''
LOGO_HEIGHT = 32

docs.title: Favicon
docs.text:
FAVICON_PATH, FAVICON_NOTIFICATION_PATH, and APPLE_TOUCH_ICON_PATH point to the default favicon files. To replace them, keep the keys but change the paths to your own assets.

# Default favicon icons (replace with your own files if needed)
FAVICON_PATH = 'favicons/favicon.ico'
FAVICON_NOTIFICATION_PATH = 'favicons/notification-favicon.ico'
APPLE_TOUCH_ICON_PATH = 'favicons/favicon.ico'

docs.title: Custom asset overrides
docs.text:
CUSTOM_* paths are optional overrides that take effect only when the files exist under seaqa-web-data. Use them if you prefer to keep defaults untouched and swap assets by placing files in the custom/ directory.

# Custom branding assets (optional overrides when files exist)
CUSTOM_LOGO_PATH = 'custom/mylogo.png'
CUSTOM_FAVICON_PATH = 'custom/favicon.ico'
CUSTOM_FAVICON_NOTIFICATION_PATH = 'custom/notification-favicon.ico'
CUSTOM_LOGIN_BG_PATH = 'custom/login-bg.jpg'

# Legacy CSS override path
BRANDING_CSS = ''
# Allow uploading branding CSS via admin UI
ENABLE_BRANDING_CSS = False
# Control whether top bar shows logout icon
SHOW_LOGOUT_ICON = False

docs.title: User management options
docs.text:
Options for registration, activation, and sign-up restrictions. These settings control the sign-up flow and whether admins are notified.

# Allow users to self-register on web UI
ENABLE_SIGNUP = False
# Auto-activate after sign-up
ACTIVATE_AFTER_REGISTRATION = True

# Send activation email when registration completes
REGISTRATION_SEND_MAIL = False
# Notify system admin after registration
NOTIFY_ADMIN_AFTER_REGISTRATION = False
# Require additional profile fields on signup
REQUIRE_DETAIL_ON_REGISTRATION = False

# List of forbidden organization prefixes
REJECT_REGISTRATION_ORG_PREFIX = []
# Regex-based org name blacklist
REJECT_REGISTRATION_ORG_RE_STR = []

# Force users to agree terms on CN deployments
CN_FORCE_USER_AGREE_TERMS = False

# Remember days for login. Default is 7
LOGIN_REMEMBER_DAYS = 7

# Maximum failed login attempts before lock
LOGIN_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 5
# Lockout window in seconds
LOGIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT = 15 * 60
# Freeze account when exceeding failures
FREEZE_USER_ON_LOGIN_FAILED = False

# minimum length for user's password
USER_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 6

# LEVEL based on four types of input:
# num, upper letter, lower letter, other symbols
# '3' means password must have at least 3 types of the above.
USER_PASSWORD_STRENGTH_LEVEL = 3

# default False, only check USER_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH
# when True, check password strength level, STRONG(or above) is allowed
USER_STRONG_PASSWORD_REQUIRED = False

# Force user to change password when admin adds/resets a user.
FORCE_PASSWORD_CHANGE = True

# Whether to allow SSO users to set a local password; default True, admin or user can set a local password by 'Reset password'
ENABLE_SSO_USER_CHANGE_PASSWORD = True

# Whether to allow LDAP users to set a local password; default False, when True, admin or user can set a local password by 'Reset password'
ENABLE_LDAP_USER_CHANGE_PASSWORD = False

# Whether or not activate inactive user on first login. Mainly used in LDAP user sync.
ACTIVATE_AFTER_FIRST_LOGIN = False

# Whether to allow users to delete their own accounts
ENABLE_DELETE_ACCOUNT = True

# Whether to allow users to update their own information
ENABLE_UPDATE_USER_INFO = True

# Age of cookie, in seconds (example: 2 weeks). Default in core is 1 day.
SESSION_COOKIE_AGE = 60 * 60 * 24

docs.title: Security settings
docs.text:
Security hardening, throttling, and login protection. Configure captchas, rate limits, and account lockout policies here.

# For security consideration, please set to match the host/domain of your site, e.g., ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['.example.com'].
# Please refer https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/ref/settings/#allowed-hosts for details.
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['.myseaticket.com']

# Enable slide captcha challenge
ENABLE_SLIDE_CAPTCHA = False
# Custom slide captcha image resource
SLIDE_CAPTCHA_IMAGE_URL = ''

# Enable Cloudflare Turnstile challenge
ENABLE_TURNSTILE = False
# Cloudflare Turnstile site key
TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY = ''
# Cloudflare Turnstile secret key
TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY = ''

# Request throttle count within period
REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_NUMBER = 3
# Request throttle period in seconds
REQUEST_RATE_LIMIT_PERIOD = 60

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
SeaTicket supports Two-Factor Authentication to enhance account security. There are two ways to enable this feature:

  1. System admin can enable it in the system settings page.
  2. Or add the following settings to seaqa_web_settings.py and restart SeaTicket.

After that, users will see a “Two-Factor Authentication” section in the user profile page and can bind an authenticator app (e.g., Google Authenticator) via QR code.

# Enable TOTP-based two factor
ENABLE_TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = False
# URL to redirect users for OTP setup when 2FA is required but not yet configured (defaults to `/profile/two_factor_authentication/setup/`)
OTP_LOGIN_URL = '/profile/two_factor_authentication/setup/'
# Force every user to enable 2FA
ENABLE_FORCE_2FA_TO_ALL_USERS = False
# Days to remember trusted devices
TWO_FACTOR_DEVICE_REMEMBER_DAYS = 90

# Enable SMS-based two factor auth
ENABLE_SMS_TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = False
# Allow SMS login
ENABLE_SMS_LOGIN = False

# SMS verification code attempt limit
SEND_SMS_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 5
# SMS verification code attempt timeout in seconds
SEND_SMS_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT = 60 * 60  # 1h

# Aliyun SMS provider configuration used by registration/SMS login flows
ALIYUN_SMS_CONFIG = {
    'accessKeyId': '',
    'accessKeySecret': '',
    'signName': '',
    'templateCode': '',
    'regionId': 'cn-hangzhou',
}

docs.title: seaticket_config.yaml
docs.text: Besides .env for general settings, the seaticket_config.yaml is used to specify the detailed configurations of the all components in SeaTicket docker.

docs.title: File structure of seaticket_config.yaml
docs.text:
seaticket_config.yaml consists of the following sections (i.e., global and name of each component):

global:
  # ... configurations for all components
seaqa-ai:
  # ... special configurations for seaqa-ai
seaqa-events:
  # ... special configurations for seaqa-events
seaqa-indexer:
  # ... special configurations for seaqa-indexer
seaqa-notification:
  # ... special configurations for seaqa-notification
seaqa-web:
  # ... special configurations for seaqa-web

docs.title: Global settings
docs.text: The global section is generally used to specify configuration items that are common to all SeaTickets components.

docs.title: Internal server URLs used for communication between SeaTicket components (cluster only)
docs.text:
In cluster mode, you need to specify the URLs used for internal communication between components via seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
  # ... other configurations
  SEATICKET_AI_INNER_SERVER_URL: http://<your seaqa-ai server host>:8887
  SEATICKET_INDEXER_INNER_SERVER_URL: http://<your seaqa-indexer server host>:8888
  SEATICKET_EVENTS_INNER_SERVER_URL: http://<your seaqa-events server host>:6001

docs.title: LLMs configurations
docs.text:
To ensure the SeaTicket service functions normally, please ensure that seaticket_config.yaml contains at least one valid LLM

For LLMs configurations, you should configure a list option LLM_MODELS in seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
  LLM_MODELS:
    # <model 1 configuration>
    - type: 'your_llm_provider' # required, please refer https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers for the details
      model: 'your_model_id' # required
      url: 'llm_endpoint' # required for some provider (or type)
      key: 'llm_secret_key' # required for non-self deploy LLM server (including OpenAI proxy)
      label: 'display_name' # optional, display name on SeaTicket chat page, default to option `model` if not set
      hidden: false # optional, hidden on SeaTicket chat page but still can be used with API calling and other components, default to `false`
      disable: false # optional, disable this LLM, default to `false`
      tier: # optional, accepts one of three values — `low`, `medium`, or `high` — and is used to specify the model's inference strength, allowing for flexible invocation across different tasks.
      price: # required only need to specify this when you need to track user token usage.
        input_tokens: 1 # dollars / 1 M tokens (non-cached)
        output_tokens: 10 # dollars / 1 M tokens

    # <model 2 configuration>
    # - type: ...

    # <model 3 configuration>
    # - type : ...

Futher information about tier of a model

  • When multiple LLMs have the same tier, the system will use only the LLM that explicitly specifies that tier, with priority given to the first entry in the LLM_MODELS list.
  • If the tier specified for a service in AI_UTILS_TIER is not defined in LLM_MODELS, then the default model in LLM_MODELS or the first valid model in the list will be used.

docs.title: Embedding model
docs.text:
To ensure the SeaTicket service functions normally, please ensure that seaticket_config.yaml has specified embedding model

The configuration of embedding models is similar to that of an element in the LLM_MODELS list:

global:
  EMBEDDING_MODEL:
    type: ...
    model: embedding_model_id
    url: embedding_model_endpoint # required for some provider (or type)

    price: 0.02 # dollars / 1 M input tokens, required only need to specify this when you need to track user token usage.

docs.title: Thought process
docs.text:
The thought process is used to display detailed debug information about LLM calls, including system prompts, context, tool call history, and cost statistics. It will be displayed in the project's Chat and Agent modules.

global:
  THOUGHT_PROCESS: # Configure which content to record in the thought process.
    enabled: false # set to `true` to record in the thought process (global switcher)
    tasks:
      enabled: true
      system_prompt: false
      user_input: true
      user_input_raw: false
    context: false
    tool_details: false

docs.text: Please refer here for the details.

docs.title: seaqa-ai settings
docs.text:
The following are the default values, normally, you don't need to make any additional settings for this part

seaqa-ai:
  COMPLETION_MAX_RETRIES: 2 # Maximum number of chating completion retries with LLM
  COMPLETION_RETRY_INTERVAL: 0.0 # Retry interval when AI chating completion fails
  TOOL_CALL_MAX_RETRIES: 2 # Maximum number of executing tool retries with LLM
  TOOL_CALL_RETRY_INTERVAL: 1.0 # Retry interval when tool executes fails
  AI_UTILS_TIER: # The tier level required to configure AI functionality (must be one of `low`, `medium`, and `high`) will be matched in `LLM_MODELS`.
    generate_ticket: low
    generate_summary: low
    rerank_relevance: medium

Model selection

  • For the chat and agent, the models typically used include:
    • Main resonance chain:
      • Chat: The model selected for the webpage (LLM_MODELS.hidden = false)
      • Agent: The defualt model in LLM_MODELS
    • An embedding model for vector search
    • A model specified by AI_UTILS_TIER.rerank_relevance for reranking search results
  • For other services (e.g., summary generation), will use the model specified in AI_UTILS_TIER

seaqa-ai:

    max_github_issues_per_run: 100 # Maximum GitHub issues analyzed per agent run
    max_analysis_steps: 10 # Maximum analysis steps per agent task
    max_handling_steps: 5 # Maximum handling steps per agent task

    enqueue_pending_events_check_intetval: 5 # Interval to check and flush pending events
    enqueue_debounce_interval: 600 # Minimum seconds between two enqueues for the same record
    enqueue_ticket_initial_debounce: 300 # Initial debounce seconds after first ticket event
    timed_scan_interval: 3600 # Timed scanner execution interval
    timed_scan_project_cooldown: 86400 # Cooldown before re-scanning the same project

docs.title: Email Sending
docs.text:
SeaTicket requires an external SMTP account to send emails. Typical emails include:

  • User password resets
  • User invitations and registration notices
  • System admin adds new members
  • System admin resets user password

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
There are two ways to configure SMTP for system-wide emails.

Environment variables / seaticket_config.yamlConfiguration file

SeaTicket reads SMTP settings from environment variables or seaticket_config.yaml for seaqa-web.

Key Description Example values EMAIL_HOST SMTP server hostname smtp.example.com EMAIL_HOST_USER Username for authentication username@example.com EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD Password for authentication password EMAIL_PORT SMTP server port 25, 465, or 587 DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL Default From header noreply@example.com SERVER_EMAIL Sender for error reporting noreply@example.com

Note

EMAIL_USE_TLS (and any SSL flag) cannot be set via environment variables or seaticket_config.yaml. Use seaqa_web_settings.py instead.

Add the following lines to seaqa_web_settings.py:

EMAIL_USE_TLS = False
EMAIL_HOST = 'smtp.example.com'
EMAIL_HOST_USER = 'username@example.com'
EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD = 'password'
EMAIL_PORT = 25
DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL = EMAIL_HOST_USER
SERVER_EMAIL = EMAIL_HOST_USER

SMTP without authentication

If you want to use the email service without authentication, leave EMAIL_HOST_USER and EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD blank ('').

TLS only

SeaTicket only exposes the EMAIL_USE_TLS flag. SSL-specific toggles are not supported; use port 465 with TLS disabled if your provider requires implicit SSL.

Restart SeaTicket after updating SMTP configuration.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
If email sending does not work, check seaqa-web logs for SMTP errors. You can also use a tool like Swaks to verify SMTP settings.

swaks --auth -tls \
  --server <EMAIL_HOST> \
  --protocol SMTP \
  --port <EMAIL_PORT> \
  --au <EMAIL_HOST_USER> \
  --ap <EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD> \
  --from <DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL> \
  --to <TO_ADDRESS> \
  --h-Subject: "Subject of the mail" \
  --body 'Test email!'
