docs.title: Confluence
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects to Confluence to sync pages from selected spaces into a project. Authentication uses Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) with the authorization code grant.

Confluence Cloud only

SeaTicket supports Confluence Cloud only. Confluence Server and Confluence Data Center are not supported.

Confluence is connected per project by a project admin from the New connection dialog. Before anyone can connect, a system administrator must register an OAuth app with Atlassian and configure SeaTicket with its credentials.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An Atlassian account with access to the Atlassian developer console.
  • A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable, because Atlassian redirects the user's browser back to the callback URL.
  • A project admin who has access to the Confluence workspace and spaces to sync.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the OAuth app
docs.text:
1. Go to the Atlassian developer console and click Create -> OAuth 2.0 integration.
  2. Enter an app name, choose the OAuth 2.0 (3LO) grant type, and create the app.
  3. Open the app's Settings and note the Client ID and Secret. You will need them in Step 4.

docs.title: Step 2: Set the callback URL
docs.text:
1. Open the app's Authorization settings.
  2. Configure OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and add the following Callback URL:
https://<seaticket-host>/confluence/oauth/callback/

Replace <seaticket-host> with your SeaTicket server hostname (the value of SEATICKET_SERVER_HOSTNAME). The callback URL must exactly match the CONFLUENCE_REDIRECT_URL configured in SeaTicket. Atlassian requires HTTPS, except for localhost during development.

docs.title: Step 3: Set the scopes
docs.text:
In the app's Permissions settings, add the Confluence API and select these scopes:

Scope Purpose search:confluence Search and read Confluence content during synchronization read:space:confluence List accessible spaces read:confluence-user Read user information returned with Confluence content report:personal-data Meet Atlassian's user-data reporting requirement

SeaTicket also requests offline_access when connecting. This allows SeaTicket to refresh its access token and keep the project connection active.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure SeaTicket
docs.text:
Configure the app credentials in the global section of seaticket_config.yaml.

Add the following to your seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
    CONFLUENCE_CLIENT_ID: "<your-atlassian-client-id>"
    CONFLUENCE_CLIENT_SECRET: "<your-atlassian-client-secret>"
    CONFLUENCE_REDIRECT_URL: "https://<seaticket-host>/confluence/oauth/callback/"

docs.title: Step 5: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web

docs.title: Step 6: Connect Confluence in the UI
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection and choose Confluence.
  3. Click Connect Confluence and, when redirected to Atlassian, sign in and approve the access request.
  4. After authorization, select the Confluence workspace to sync.
  5. Optionally select one or more spaces. Leave this empty to sync all spaces that the authorized account can access in the selected workspace.
  6. Save the connection.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The callback URL does not match. The value of CONFLUENCE_REDIRECT_URL must exactly match the Callback URL in the Atlassian app, including the scheme and trailing slash.
  • "Confluence OAuth settings are invalid." At least one of the CONFLUENCE_* settings is empty in the configuration loaded by seaqa-web. Check the credentials and restart the container.
  • No workspace is listed. Confirm that the authorized Atlassian account can access at least one Confluence Cloud workspace and that the app was granted the required Confluence scopes.
  • A space is missing. The authorized account must have permission to view that space in Confluence.
  • The connection later stops syncing with an authorization error. The user may have revoked access, or the Atlassian refresh token may have expired. Reconnect Confluence from the project's Connections page.

docs.title: Discord
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects to Discord to sync posts from a forum channel into a project. Authorization uses Discord's OAuth2 flow, which adds the SeaTicket bot to your server.

Discord is connected per project by a project admin from the New connection dialog. Before anyone can connect, a system administrator must create a Discord application, add a bot to it, and configure SeaTicket with the credentials.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Manage Server permission on the Discord server you want to sync.
  • A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable, because Discord redirects the user's browser back to the redirect URL.
  • At least one forum channel on the server. SeaTicket syncs forum channels only; text and voice channels cannot be selected.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Discord application
docs.text:
1. Open the Discord Developer Portal and click New Application.
  2. Enter a name and create the application.
  3. Open the OAuth2 page and note the Client ID. Under Client Secret, click Reset Secret and copy the value.

You will need both in Step 4.

docs.title: Step 2: Add a bot and copy its token
docs.text:
1. Open the Bot page.
  2. If no bot exists yet, click Add Bot and confirm.
  3. Under Privileged Gateway Intents, enable Message Content Intent. SeaTicket reads message content through the Discord API, and Discord returns messages with empty content without this intent.
  4. Click Reset Token and copy the token that Discord shows.

The token is shown only once

Copy the bot token as soon as it is displayed. If you lose it, reset the token again; that invalidates the previous one, so update DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN and restart SeaTicket afterwards.

docs.title: Step 3: Set the redirect URL
docs.text:
Under OAuth2 -> Redirects, add the following and save your changes:

https://<seaticket-host>/discord/oauth/callback/

Replace <seaticket-host> with your SeaTicket server hostname (the value of SEATICKET_SERVER_HOSTNAME). The URL must exactly match the DISCORD_REDIRECT_URL configured in SeaTicket.

SeaTicket requests the bot and identify OAuth scopes during installation. Do not create a separate bot invite URL; use the SeaTicket connection flow described in Step 6.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure SeaTicket
docs.text:
Add the following values under the existing global section of seaticket_config.yaml. Both the web service and indexer need access to the bot token:

global:
    DISCORD_CLIENT_ID: "<your-client-id>"
    DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET: "<your-client-secret>"
    DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN: "<your-bot-token>"
    DISCORD_REDIRECT_URL: "https://<seaticket-host>/discord/oauth/callback/"

docs.title: Step 5: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web and seaqa-indexer for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web seaqa-indexer

docs.title: Step 6: Connect Discord in the UI
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection and choose Discord.
  3. Click Install Discord Bot and, on Discord, choose the server and authorize the bot.
  4. Back in SeaTicket, select the Channel to sync and save the connection.

The permissions SeaTicket needs (View Channel and Read Message History) are requested as part of this authorization, so you do not need to set permissions for the app in the Developer Portal.

Only forum channels are listed

The Channel list contains forum channels only. If it is empty, the server has no forum channel, or the bot was not granted access to it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Discord OAuth settings are invalid." At least one of DISCORD_CLIENT_ID, DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET, and DISCORD_REDIRECT_URL is empty when seaqa-web reads its configuration. Check the values under the global section of seaticket_config.yaml and restart the services. Values in .env are not automatically forwarded to the containers.
  • "Invalid Discord OAuth state." or "Discord server information was not returned." The authorization flow was interrupted, or no server was selected. Start the connection again from Install Discord Bot.
  • "Failed to authorize Discord." The Client Secret or the redirect URL does not match what is registered in the Discord application. Check both, then restart seaqa-web.
  • The Channel list is empty. The server has no forum channel, or the bot was not granted access to it. Add a forum channel or install the bot again.
  • Synced posts have no content. The bot is missing the Message Content Intent. Enable it under Privileged Gateway Intents on the Bot page.
  • Bot token rejected. SeaTicket returns Invalid Discord bot token when DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN is wrong or was reset in the Developer Portal. Copy the current token, update the setting, and restart seaqa-web.
  • Rate limiting. Discord returns Discord API rate limited. Please try again later when it throttles the request. Wait a moment and try again.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects to GitHub to sync issues into a project. Authentication uses a GitHub App. SeaTicket signs a JWT with the app's private key and exchanges it for an installation access token.

github.com only

SeaTicket uses the github.com and api.github.com hosts, and these cannot be changed. GitHub Enterprise Server (self-hosted) and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency on a *.ghe.com domain are therefore not supported.

GitHub is connected per project by a project admin from the New connection dialog. Before anyone can connect, a system administrator must create a GitHub App and configure SeaTicket with the app's credentials.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Admin or owner access to the GitHub account or organization whose repositories you want to sync.
  • A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable, because GitHub redirects the user's browser back to the setup URL.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the GitHub App
docs.text:
1. In GitHub, open Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps and click New GitHub App. To create an app owned by a personal account, use the new GitHub App page; for an organization, open https://github.com/organizations/<organization>/settings/apps/new.
  2. Enter a name and your SeaTicket URL as the homepage URL.
  3. Enter https://<seaticket-host>/github/installation-setup/ as the Redirect URI.
  4. Leave Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation unchecked. Enabling it hides the Setup URL field that SeaTicket depends on.

Expire user authorization tokens

SeaTicket authenticates as the app installation rather than on behalf of a user, so this setting has no effect on it. It governs user access tokens only, while installation tokens expire after an hour and are renewed on demand.

docs.title: Step 2: Set the setup URL
docs.text:
Under Post installation, enter the following as the Setup URL:

https://<seaticket-host>/github/installation-setup/

GitHub redirects users here after they install the app, which is how SeaTicket records the installation. Select Redirect on update so the setup URL also runs when repositories are added to or removed from an installation.

docs.title: Step 3: Set the permissions
docs.text:
Under Repository permissions, grant:

Permission Access Purpose Issues Read and write Read issues and comments, and update them when the AI agent acts on a ticket Metadata Read-only Required by GitHub for every app

Under Organization permissions, grant:

Permission Access Purpose Issue types Read-only Read organization issue types for mapping them to agent task types

Issue types

Reading issue types requires the Issue types organization permission above. They are an organization-level feature, so they only exist on repositories owned by an organization.

docs.title: Step 4: Create the app
docs.text: Under Where can this GitHub App be installed?, select Only on this account if the app will only be installed on the account that owns it, or Any account to let other accounts install it. Then click Create GitHub App.

docs.title: Step 5: Note the App ID and generate a private key
docs.text:
1. On the app's settings page, note the App ID (not the Client ID, which SeaTicket does not use).
  2. Note the app's URL slug. GitHub derives it from the app name and shows it at https://github.com/apps/<slug>; the slug is not always identical to the name, since spaces become hyphens.
  3. Under Private keys, click Generate a private key. GitHub downloads a .pem file, and this is the only opportunity to download it.

docs.title: Place the private key
docs.text:
Copy the .pem file to the host directory that is already mounted into the seaqa-web container:

cp <downloaded>.private-key.pem /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/conf/github-app.pem

That host directory is mounted at /opt/seaticket/conf, so the path inside the container is /opt/seaticket/conf/github-app.pem, and no change to the compose volumes is needed.

The file has to be readable by the account the container runs as. Check its owner and permissions after copying it, for example with ls -l.

docs.title: Set the app credentials
docs.text:
Add the following to your seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
    GITHUB_APP_NAME: "<your-app-slug>"
    GITHUB_APP_ID: "<your-app-id>"
    GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH: "/opt/seaticket/conf/github-app.pem"

A wrong private key path fails silently

If GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH does not point to a readable file, SeaTicket starts with an empty private key rather than reporting an error. The mistake surfaces later, when GitHub API calls fail.

docs.title: Step 7: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web

docs.title: Step 8: Install the app and connect in the UI
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection and choose GitHub.
  3. Click Install GitHub app and, on GitHub, grant access to the repositories you want to sync.
  4. Back in SeaTicket, select the Repository to sync and save the connection.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The install link returns 404. GITHUB_APP_NAME must be the app's URL slug, not its display name. Compare it with the last part of https://github.com/apps/<slug>.
  • "The app has not been installed on the sea-ticket." SeaTicket has no installation record, which means the setup URL callback did not complete. Check that the Setup URL points at https://<seaticket-host>/github/installation-setup/ and is reachable from the internet, then install the app again.
  • Installing the app does not redirect back to SeaTicket. If the app is already installed on the organization, GitHub skips the setup flow and does not call the Setup URL. Open the installation's settings, change Repository access to another option and then back, and save; because Redirect on update is enabled, GitHub then sends the setup redirect and SeaTicket records the installation.
  • Syncing fails with a token error. SeaTicket could not read the private key. Check that GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH points to a readable .pem file inside the container and that GITHUB_APP_ID holds the numeric App ID.
  • Issue types are not listed. Issue types only exist on repositories owned by an organization. Check that the app is granted the Issue types organization permission described in Step 3.

docs.title: Gmail
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects Gmail mailboxes and aliases to projects using OAuth 2.0. Connections can send email replies and perform mailbox operations through the Gmail API. Both Gmail accounts and Google Workspace users with Gmail enabled can authorize a mailbox.

By default, use the unified OAuth client: a system administrator does not need to register a Google application or configure a client ID and secret. Deployments that need their own application identity can use their own OAuth client.

docs.title: Supported connection types
docs.text:
Type Authorization and behavior Personal Authorize the Google account whose Gmail mailbox the project should use. This can be a Gmail account or a Google Workspace user account. Alias Authorize the account that owns the mailbox, then use an alias configured and permitted as a sending identity for that mailbox. An alias is not a separate sign-in account or mailbox.

Gmail service accounts are not supported

Gmail connections use user-delegated OAuth authorization. Service-account authentication, including domain-wide delegation, is not supported. There is no separate Gmail shared-mailbox connection type; shared-mailbox connections are available for Microsoft 365 only.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable over HTTPS, because Google redirects the user's browser back to SeaTicket.
  • A project admin who can complete authorization with a Google account that has access to the intended Gmail mailbox.
  • For an alias, configure the address as an allowed sending identity in Gmail before connecting it. See Send emails from a different address or alias.
  • Access to Google Cloud Console only if you choose to manage your own OAuth client.

docs.title: Connect Gmail using the unified client
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection, choose Email, and select Gmail as the provider.
  3. Choose a personal-mailbox or alias connection, as appropriate.
  4. Start OAuth authorization and sign in to the Google account that owns the mailbox. For an alias, authorize its underlying mailbox account, not the alias address as a separate account.
  5. Review the requested access and approve it. Your organization's Google Workspace policies may require administrator approval.
  6. Back in the connection dialog, verify the mailbox and sender address. For an alias connection, specify the configured alias as the sender, then save the connection.

Project-admin permission is required to create the connection; it does not mean the authorized Google account must be the same address as the SeaTicket administrator's login.

docs.title: Use your own OAuth client
docs.text:
This is optional. A self-managed client may be appropriate when you need:

  • Your own product branding: use an application name, logo, and policy links that identify your business on Google's consent screen, especially for a public commercial service.
  • An organization-internal application: eligible Google Workspace organizations can restrict the app to internal users. Internal-only apps may qualify for verification exceptions; this does not remove OAuth consent or organization access-policy requirements.
  • Independent security and compliance administration: control the app registration, credentials, permissions, and lifecycle under your organization's policies. A self-managed client alone does not guarantee a particular token-routing or data-residency arrangement.
  • Independent API quota management: manage the Google Cloud project and its project-level quotas separately rather than sharing a client project's quota. Per-user and other Gmail API limits still apply.

Review Google's OAuth verification requirements and exceptions and Gmail API usage limits. External apps requesting restricted scopes may require verification and, where applicable, a security assessment. Internal status is not a blanket exemption from all security requirements.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Google OAuth client
docs.text:
1. In Google Cloud Console, create or select a project.
  2. Enable the Gmail API for the project.
  3. Configure the OAuth consent screen. If the application is external, add test users while the application remains in testing.
  4. Open APIs & Services -> Credentials and create an OAuth client ID for a Web application.
  5. Add the following authorized redirect URI:
https://<seaticket-host>/api/v1/connections/email/oauth/callback/

Replace <seaticket-host> with the public SeaTicket URL. SeaTicket derives this URL from SEAQA_WEB_SERVICE_URL. It must exactly match the redirect URI registered in Google, including the scheme and trailing slash.

  1. Copy the client ID and client secret.

Gmail mailbox access uses the following scopes:

Scope Purpose https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify Read and modify mailbox messages, including moving messages to trash or spam https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send Send email replies https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.settings.basic Discover mailbox sending identities, including configured aliases

Google may require OAuth consent-screen verification before non-test users can authorize scopes that it classifies as sensitive or restricted. Follow the requirements shown in Google Cloud Console for your application.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure SeaTicket
docs.text:
Merge the following into the existing global section of seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
    GOOGLE_EMAIL_CLIENT_ID: "<your-google-client-id>"
    GOOGLE_EMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET: "<your-google-client-secret>"

docs.title: Step 3: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web

Then create the connection using the mailbox or alias authorization flow described above, with your self-managed client.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Email OAuth provider is not configured." If you use a self-managed client, confirm that both GOOGLE_EMAIL_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_EMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET are present under global in seaticket_config.yaml, then restart seaqa-web. Adding them to .env alone does not configure the container.
  • The redirect URI does not match with your own client. The redirect URI in Google Cloud Console must exactly match https://<seaticket-host>/api/v1/connections/email/oauth/callback/.
  • The authorization popup does not open. Allow popups for the SeaTicket site in the browser, then start authorization again.
  • The callback reports that the request is missing or expired. OAuth authorization requests expire after 10 minutes. Start the authorization again and complete it in the same browser session.
  • Google does not return a refresh token. Confirm that the redirect URI is correct and that the user approved the consent request. Revoke the application's access in the Google account if needed, then authorize again.
  • The sender address cannot be discovered. Verify that the authorized Google account has a usable Gmail sending identity and granted the required Gmail API permissions.
  • An alias cannot send replies. Confirm that the address is configured and verified as an allowed sending identity for the authorized mailbox. Authorizing an account does not grant permission to send from an arbitrary address.
  • Authorization is blocked by your organization. Ask your Google Workspace administrator to review the OAuth app and requested scopes under the organization's access policies. Using an internal client does not bypass those policies.

docs.title: Jira
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects to Jira to sync issues into a project. Authentication uses Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) with the authorization code grant.

Atlassian Cloud only

The Jira integration supports Atlassian Cloud only. Jira Server and Jira Data Center are not supported.

Jira is connected per project by a project admin from the New connection dialog. Before anyone can connect, a system administrator must register an OAuth app with Atlassian and configure SeaTicket with its credentials.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An Atlassian account with access to the Atlassian developer console.
  • A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable, because Atlassian redirects the user's browser back to the callback URL.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the OAuth app
docs.text:
1. Go to the Atlassian developer console and click Create → OAuth 2.0 integration.
  2. Enter a name for your app, agree to the developer terms, and create it.
  3. Open the app's Settings and note the Client ID and Secret, which you will need in Step 4.

docs.title: Step 2: Set the callback URL
docs.text:
In the app's OAuth 2.0 (3LO) settings, add the following as the Callback URL:

https://<seaticket-host>/jira/oauth/callback/

Replace <seaticket-host> with your SeaTicket server hostname (the value of SEATICKET_SERVER_HOSTNAME). The callback URL must exactly match the JIRA_REDIRECT_URL configured in SeaTicket. Atlassian requires HTTPS, except for localhost during development.

docs.title: Step 3: Set the scopes
docs.text:
In the app's Permissions settings, add the Jira API and select the following scopes:

Scope Purpose read:jira-work Read issues and projects read:jira-user Read user information

SeaTicket also requests offline_access automatically when connecting, so it can obtain a refresh token and keep the connection valid. This scope is sent in the authorization request and does not need to be added to the app.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure SeaTicket
docs.text:
Configure the app credentials in the global section of seaticket_config.yaml.

Add the following to your seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
    JIRA_CLIENT_ID: "<your-atlassian-client-id>"
    JIRA_CLIENT_SECRET: "<your-atlassian-client-secret>"
    JIRA_REDIRECT_URL: "https://<seaticket-host>/jira/oauth/callback/"

docs.title: Step 5: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web

docs.title: Step 6: Connect Jira in the UI
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection and choose Jira.
  3. Click Connect Jira and, when redirected to Atlassian, sign in and approve the access request.
  4. After you grant access, pick the Jira site and project to sync and save the connection.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The callback URL does not match. The value of JIRA_REDIRECT_URL must exactly match the Callback URL registered in the Atlassian app, including the scheme and trailing slash.
  • "Jira OAuth settings are invalid." The three JIRA_* settings are empty in the config that seaqa-web actually loaded. Check that the credentials are present under the global section of seaticket_config.yaml and that the container was restarted.
  • The connection fails after you grant access. Ensure your SeaTicket hostname is publicly reachable, because Atlassian redirects the browser back to the callback URL.

docs.title: Linear
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects to Linear to sync issues into a project. Authentication uses Linear's OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow.

Linear is connected per project by a project admin from the New connection dialog. Before anyone can connect, a system administrator must register an OAuth application with Linear and configure SeaTicket with its credentials.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Workspace administrator access to a Linear workspace. Only workspace admins can create OAuth applications.
  • A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable, because Linear redirects the user's browser back to the callback URL.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the OAuth app
docs.text:
1. In Linear, open Settings → API → OAuth applications and create a new application. You can also open the new application page directly.
  2. Fill in the application details and create it in the workspace whose issues you want to sync. A new application is private by default, so it can only be authorized from the workspace it was created in; enable Public if you need other workspaces to authorize it.
  3. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the application page. You will need them in Step 3.

Note

Linear applications do not require you to select scopes. SeaTicket sends no scope parameter when connecting, so Linear grants its default read access, which is sufficient for syncing issues.

Choosing a workspace for the application

From Linear's OAuth 2.0 documentation:

It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

docs.title: Step 2: Set the callback URL
docs.text:
Add the following to the application's Callback URLs:

https://<seaticket-host>/linear/oauth/callback/

Replace <seaticket-host> with your SeaTicket server hostname (the value of SEATICKET_SERVER_HOSTNAME). The callback URL must exactly match the LINEAR_REDIRECT_URL configured in SeaTicket. You can register more than one callback URL; enter each on its own line.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure SeaTicket
docs.text:
Configure the application credentials in the global section of seaticket_config.yaml.

Add the following to your seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
    LINEAR_CLIENT_ID: "<your-linear-client-id>"
    LINEAR_CLIENT_SECRET: "<your-linear-client-secret>"
    LINEAR_REDIRECT_URL: "https://<seaticket-host>/linear/oauth/callback/"

docs.title: Step 4: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web

docs.title: Step 5: Connect Linear in the UI
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection and choose Linear.
  3. Click Connect Linear and, when redirected to Linear, sign in and approve the access request.
  4. After you grant access, select the Linear Team to sync and save the connection.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The callback URL does not match. The value of LINEAR_REDIRECT_URL must exactly match one of the callback URLs registered in the Linear application, including the scheme and trailing slash.
  • "Linear OAuth settings are invalid." At least one of the LINEAR_* settings is empty when seaqa-web reads its configuration. Check that the credentials are present under the global section of seaticket_config.yaml and that the container was restarted.
  • The connection fails after you grant access. Ensure your SeaTicket hostname is publicly reachable, because Linear redirects the browser back to the callback URL.
  • You cannot select a Team. SeaTicket only lists teams after Linear has been authorized for the project. Complete the authorization to enable the Team field.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 and Outlook
docs.text:
SeaTicket connects Microsoft 365 and Outlook mailboxes, aliases, and Microsoft 365 shared mailboxes to projects using OAuth 2.0. Connections can send email replies and perform mailbox operations through Microsoft Graph.

By default, use the unified OAuth client: a system administrator does not need to register a Microsoft Entra application or configure a client ID and secret. Deployments that need their own application identity can use their own OAuth client.

docs.title: Supported connection types
docs.text: Type Authorization and behavior Personal Authorize a user with a Microsoft 365 or Outlook mailbox. This connection type is not limited to consumer Microsoft accounts; organization user mailboxes are also supported. Alias Authorize the user who owns the mailbox and use an alias that the mailbox is permitted to send from. An alias is not a separate mailbox or sign-in account. Shared mailbox Authorize a Microsoft 365 user who has access to the shared mailbox, then specify the shared mailbox address. Do not sign in directly as the shared mailbox. This type is available for Microsoft 365, not consumer Outlook accounts.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A SeaTicket hostname that is publicly reachable over HTTPS, because Microsoft redirects the user's browser back to SeaTicket.
  • A project admin who can complete authorization with a Microsoft account that has access to the intended mailbox.
  • For an alias, the address must belong to the authorized mailbox, and the organization's Exchange Online settings must permit sending from aliases where applicable.
  • For a shared mailbox, an organization administrator must grant the authorizing user the required mailbox access and sending rights, such as Full Access and Send As, or Send on Behalf where appropriate. OAuth consent alone does not grant these rights.
  • Access to the Microsoft Entra admin center only if you choose to manage your own OAuth client or need tenant-admin approval.

docs.title: Connect using the unified client
docs.text:
1. Sign in as a project admin and open the project's Connections.
  2. Click New connection, choose Email, and select Microsoft as the provider.
  3. Choose the connection type: personal mailbox, alias, or shared mailbox.
  4. Start OAuth authorization. For a personal mailbox or alias, sign in as the mailbox owner. For a shared mailbox, sign in as a user with delegated access to that mailbox.
  5. Review the requested access and approve it. Your organization's tenant policies may require administrator consent.
  6. Back in the connection dialog, verify the mailbox and sender address. For an alias, specify the permitted alias; for a shared mailbox, specify its address. Save the connection.

Project-admin permission is required to create the connection. The authorizing Microsoft account does not have to use the same address as the SeaTicket administrator's login.

Shared mailbox permissions

Shared-mailbox access uses delegated user authorization. The authorizing user must have mailbox permissions in Exchange Online as well as the required Microsoft Graph consent. An alias does not have its own mailbox; a shared mailbox does. See Microsoft's guidance on shared and delegated mail access and sending mail from another user.

docs.title: Use your own OAuth client
docs.text:
This is optional. A self-managed client may be appropriate for:

  • Product branding and trust: manage your own application identity, publisher information, and consent experience for a commercial service.
  • Internal deployments: register an application restricted to the intended organization and manage it through the tenant's consent and access policies. Administrator approval may still be required.
  • Security and compliance: control the app registration, credentials, permissions, and lifecycle under your organization's policies. A self-managed client alone does not guarantee a particular token-routing or data-residency arrangement.
  • Independent application administration: manage usage and service limits separately where Microsoft applies app-specific limits. Microsoft Graph also applies user-, tenant-, and service-specific throttling; a separate client does not remove those limits.

For details, see Microsoft's application registration guidance, consent framework, and Microsoft Graph throttling guidance.

docs.title: Step 1: Register a Microsoft Entra application
docs.text:
1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center and go to App registrations.
  2. Click New registration, enter an application name, and select the account types your deployment needs.
  3. Under Redirect URI, select Web and enter:
https://<seaticket-host>/api/v1/connections/email/oauth/callback/

Replace <seaticket-host> with the public SeaTicket URL. SeaTicket derives this URL from SEAQA_WEB_SERVICE_URL. It must exactly match the redirect URI registered in Microsoft Entra, including the scheme and trailing slash.

  1. Create the registration and copy its Application (client) ID.
  2. Open Certificates & secrets, create a client secret, and copy its Value. The value is shown only once.
  3. Open API permissions -> Add a permission -> Microsoft Graph -> Delegated permissions, then add the following permissions:
Permission Purpose User.Read Discover the authorized mailbox identity Mail.ReadWrite Read and manage mailbox messages Mail.Send Send email replies Mail.ReadWrite.Shared Read and manage shared-mailbox messages when using shared-mailbox connections Mail.Send.Shared Send mail from a shared mailbox when using shared-mailbox connections
  1. Grant tenant admin consent if your Microsoft Entra tenant requires it.

For user-mailbox authorization, SeaTicket also requests the standard openid, profile, email, and offline_access scopes. Shared-mailbox authorization uses the delegated shared-mail permissions and offline_access. The latter allows SeaTicket to refresh authorization without requiring the user to sign in again for each operation. Add permissions for the connection types you intend to use; mailbox access and sending rights must also be configured in Exchange Online.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure SeaTicket
docs.text:
Merge the following into the existing global section of seaticket_config.yaml:

global:
    MICROSOFT_EMAIL_CLIENT_ID: "<your-microsoft-application-client-id>"
    MICROSOFT_EMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET: "<your-microsoft-client-secret>"

docs.title: Step 3: Restart SeaTicket
docs.text:
Restart seaqa-web for the new settings to take effect:

docker compose restart seaqa-web

Then create the connection using the mailbox, alias, or shared-mailbox authorization flow described above, with your self-managed client.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Email OAuth provider is not configured." If you use a self-managed client, confirm that both MICROSOFT_EMAIL_CLIENT_ID and MICROSOFT_EMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET are present under global in seaticket_config.yaml, then restart seaqa-web. Adding them to .env alone does not configure the container.
  • The redirect URI does not match with your own client. The redirect URI in Microsoft Entra must exactly match https://<seaticket-host>/api/v1/connections/email/oauth/callback/.
  • The authorization popup does not open. Allow popups for the SeaTicket site in the browser, then start authorization again.
  • The callback reports that the request is missing or expired. OAuth authorization requests expire after 10 minutes. Start the authorization again and complete it in the same browser session.
  • Microsoft does not return a refresh token. Confirm that the redirect URI is correct, offline_access was approved, and the user approved the consent request. Revoke the application's access if needed, then authorize again.
  • The sender address cannot be discovered. Verify that the authorized account has a usable Microsoft 365 or Outlook mailbox and granted the required Microsoft Graph permissions.
  • A shared mailbox cannot be accessed or cannot send replies. Confirm that authorization was completed by a user with access to the shared mailbox, the shared mailbox address is correct, and both delegated Graph permissions and Exchange Online mailbox/sending rights have been granted.
  • An alias cannot send replies. Check that the alias belongs to the authorized mailbox and that sending from aliases is enabled where required by the organization's Exchange Online configuration.
  • Administrator approval is required. Ask the tenant administrator to review the application and requested permissions. Using a unified or self-managed client does not bypass tenant consent policies.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
SeaTicket can connect to third-party services and sync their content into projects. Integrations use OAuth or provider-specific application authentication. Register an app with the service provider and configure its credentials as described on the integration's page. Email connections can instead use the unified OAuth client without registering your own app, or an optional client that you manage.

Configure your own integration credentials in the global section of seaticket_config.yaml, not in .env. Merge settings into the existing global section rather than creating a duplicate YAML key. See each integration's page for the required settings and services to restart.

Migrating integration credentials from .env

Docker Compose does not automatically inject every value from the project .env into containers. The deployment templates no longer forward third-party integration credentials from .env. Before upgrading, move any existing integration credentials, including all four DISCORD_* settings, to global in seaticket_config.yaml and restart the affected services. If you previously added custom environment mappings, remove those mappings and recreate the affected containers so stale or empty environment values do not override the YAML settings.

Integration Description Jira Sync Jira issues using Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) Linear Sync Linear issues using OAuth 2.0 GitHub Sync GitHub issues using a GitHub App Confluence Sync Confluence Cloud pages using Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) Discord Sync Discord forum posts using an OAuth2 bot Gmail Connect a Gmail mailbox or alias using a unified or self-managed OAuth client Microsoft 365 and Outlook Connect a mailbox, alias, or Microsoft 365 shared mailbox using a unified or self-managed OAuth client

docs.title: Setup Notification Server
docs.text: seaqa-notification is the WebSocket service used to deliver realtime notifications to the browser, including connection syncing events, user notifications.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The notification flow is:

  1. seaqa-indexer publishes a message to the Redis Pub/Sub channel connection_sync after a connection sync finishes.
  2. seaqa-notification subscribes to connection_sync, keeps project WebSocket subscriptions in memory, and forwards the message to clients of the matching project_uuid.
  3. seaqa-web requests project-notification-jwt-token, opens a WebSocket connection, subscribes to the current project, and shows a success or failure toast when the message arrives.

The sync notification payload is:

{
  "project_uuid": "d918792d-f3f0-4e62-afe9-9ae0595a145e",
  "connection_id": 25,
  "status": "completed",
  "type": "connection-sync"
}

docs.title: WebSocket Authentication
docs.text:
When a user enters a project page, seaqa-web requests project-notification-jwt-token to validate permissions and issue a JWT token.

  • The token is valid for 3 days.
  • The browser connects to seaqa-notification with this token.
  • seaqa-notification validates the token and stores the WebSocket connection in memory.
  • ExpirationScheduler tracks token expiration time for each subscribed project.
  • When a token expires, seaqa-notification sends a jwt-expired message to the browser.
  • The browser then requests a new token and re-subscribes to the project.

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text: The SeaTicket Docker deployment uses Caddy, not nginx, as the reverse proxy. For this reason, you do not need to manually edit an nginx.conf file when you deploy seaqa-notification with the provided Docker Compose files.

docs.title: Download the compose file
docs.text:
Download seaqa-notification.yml into the same directory as the other SeaTicket compose files:

cd /opt/seaticket
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seaqa-notification.yml

docs.title: Modify .env
docs.text:
Add the following settings:

ENABLE_NOTIFICATION_SERVER=true

seaqa-web connects to /ws on the current public SeaTicket host. This notification path is fixed and is not configured through .env or seaticket_config.yaml.

docs.title: Update COMPOSE_FILE
docs.text:
Add seaqa-notification.yml to COMPOSE_FILE:

COMPOSE_FILE='caddy.yml,seaqa-web.yml,seaqa-notification.yml'

Then start or restart the services:

docker compose up -d

docs.title: Reverse proxy behavior
docs.text:
In the Docker example, seaqa-notification.yml adds a Caddy path route for /ws, and seaqa-web.yml continues to serve the rest of the site.

You only need to make sure that:

  • seaqa-notification can access the same Redis and JWT_PRIVATE_KEY as the other SeaTicket services.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The following assumptions and conventions are used in the rest of this document:

  • /opt/seaticket is the directory for storing SeaTicket Docker Compose files and .env. If you choose a different directory, adjust all paths accordingly.
  • SeaTicket uses Docker bind mounts to persist data on the host. The default host paths are /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data for application data, /opt/seaticket-mysql/db for MySQL/MariaDB, /opt/seadb-data for SeaDB, /opt/seasearch-data for SeaSearch, and /opt/caddy-data for Caddy. It is recommended to keep these defaults. If you change them, account for the new paths when following these instructions.
  • SeaTicket configuration files, application logs, and locally stored attachments are kept under /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data, in the conf, logs, and data/attachments directories, respectively. This directory is mounted at /shared inside the SeaTicket containers.

docs.title: Download Deployment Files
docs.text:
SeaTicket uses .env and Docker Compose files from the same directory. Download the standard deployment files:

mkdir -p /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/conf
cd /opt/seaticket

wget -O .env https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/env
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/caddy.yml
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seadb.yml
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seaqa-web.yml
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seaqa-ai.yml
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seaqa-events.yml
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seaqa-indexer.yml
wget https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seasearch.yml
wget -O seaticket-data/conf/seaticket_config.yaml https://manual.seaticket.ai/0.9/repo/docker/seaticket_config.yaml

docs.title: Configure .env
docs.text: Edit /opt/seaticket/.env. For a standard deployment, change only the required settings below and leave the remaining template values at their defaults.

docs.title: Required Settings
docs.text:
Variable Description Value SEATICKET_SERVER_HOSTNAME Public hostname or domain of the SeaTicket server. Required JWT_PRIVATE_KEY Random string of at least 32 characters. Generate with pwgen -s 40 1. Required SECRET_KEY Random string of at least 32 characters. Back it up and do not change it after deployment. Required MYSQL_DB_PASSWORD Password for the SeaTicket MariaDB user. Required INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD Password for the bundled MariaDB root user. Required on first deployment only INIT_SEADB_ROOT_PASSWORD Optional separate SeaDB root password. When empty, uses INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD for initialization. Optional INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL Email address for the first SeaTicket team administrator. Required on first deployment only INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD Password for the first SeaTicket team administrator. Required on first deployment only SEADB_USERNAME Optional separate SeaDB API username. When empty, uses MYSQL_DB_USER (default seaticket). Optional SEADB_PASSWORD Optional separate SeaDB API password. When empty, uses MYSQL_DB_PASSWORD. Optional SEASEARCH_TOKEN Base64 authorization token for the SeaSearch account. Required

By default, the first SeaSearch account uses the first team administrator credentials. Generate the token after setting INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL and INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD:

echo -n 'INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL:INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD' | base64

Replace the placeholders in the command with their actual values and assign the result to SEASEARCH_TOKEN.

docs.title: Common Optional Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default SEATICKET_SERVER_PROTOCOL Public server protocol: http or https. http TIME_ZONE Time zone used by containers. UTC INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_NAME Name of the first SeaTicket team. SeaTicket ENABLE_NOTIFICATION_SERVER Enable the WebSocket notification service. false LOG_TO_STDOUT Write component logs to container standard output. false

docs.title: Database Settings
docs.text:
The standard Compose deployment includes MariaDB and initializes it automatically. Do not create the database, database user, or tables manually.

Variable Description Default MYSQL_DB_HOST MySQL/MariaDB hostname; use db for bundled MariaDB. db MYSQL_DB_PORT MariaDB port. 3306 MYSQL_DB_USER SeaTicket database user. seaticket MYSQL_DB_NAME SeaTicket database name. seaticket_db

On first startup, the entrypoint runs /scripts/init_mysql.py. This script uses PyMySQL and INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD to create the database and user, then imports sql/mysql.sql with the mysql client if the database has no tables. Credentials for the import are stored in a private temporary option file that is removed afterward. It records successful initialization in seaqa-web-data/.mysql-initialized under SEATICKET_VOLUME. Subsequent startups use the application account and skip root initialization. Keep the MySQL data and SeaTicket application data persistent and back up both database passwords.

For an external MySQL/MariaDB server, set MYSQL_DB_HOST and MYSQL_DB_PORT to its address and provide that server's root password in INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD for the first initialization. The server must allow root connections from the seaqa-web container and permit database creation, user creation, and grants. Automatic initialization is supported regardless of the hostname. When the bundled database is not needed, remove the db service from seaqa-web.yml and remove its depends_on entries from all enabled Compose files, including seaqa-web.yml, seaqa-ai.yml, seaqa-events.yml, seaqa-indexer.yml, and seaqa-web-portal.yml if enabled.

docs.title: SeaDB Settings
docs.text:
By default, SeaDB uses INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD as its initial root password and MYSQL_DB_USER / MYSQL_DB_PASSWORD as its application credentials. You can leave INIT_SEADB_ROOT_PASSWORD, SEADB_USERNAME, and SEADB_PASSWORD empty. Set any of these variables to use separate SeaDB credentials; each override is independent.

On first startup with an empty or missing data directory, the SeaDB container maps the resolved initialization password to SEADB_ROOT_PASSWORD and runs sea-db init to create the root administrator. The seaqa-web container then authenticates as root to create the resolved application account, assigning default_role. Compose supplies the resolved username as SEADB_USER inside all SeaTicket containers. SeaTicket services use the application credentials with HTTP Basic authentication to access SeaDB.

For an existing deployment that used the first team administrator credentials for SeaDB, explicitly set SEADB_USERNAME and SEADB_PASSWORD to the existing SeaDB account values before updating the Compose files. The new defaults do not modify existing accounts. JWT_PRIVATE_KEY is required by the SeaDB service but is not an API access token.

docs.title: Cache Settings
docs.text:
The standard deployment includes Redis. No changes are required for normal use.

Variable Description Default REDIS_HOST Bundled Redis service hostname. redis REDIS_PORT Redis port. 6379 REDIS_PASSWORD Redis password. (none)

docs.title: Storage Settings
docs.text:
Leave the storage settings at their defaults for a local-disk deployment without S3:

Variable Description Default ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND Attachment storage backend: disk or s3. Used by the web service, IO service, indexer, and optional portal. disk SS_STORAGE_TYPE Optional SeaSearch storage override: disk or s3. If unset or empty, uses ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND; if both are unset or empty, uses disk. Follows ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND

Attachment storage with disk backend

With ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=disk, attachments are saved to ${SEATICKET_VOLUME}/data/attachments on the host (/opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/data/attachments by default). This directory contains project_attachments and connection_attachments and must be included in backups.

Inside the web and indexer containers, /opt/seaticket/data links to /shared/data. The image fixes the attachment root at /opt/seaticket/data/attachments; no attachment-root setting is required in .env or seaticket_config.yaml. All attachment services must share the same SEATICKET_VOLUME.

When SeaSearch uses disk, its data is persisted under ${SS_DATA_PATH} on the host (/opt/seasearch-data by default).

Existing deployments

Existing S3 deployments must explicitly set ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 before adopting these deployment files. SeaSearch follows that setting unless SS_STORAGE_TYPE is explicitly set. Changing a storage backend does not migrate existing attachments or search data.

docs.title: Use S3 as the storage backend
docs.text:
Skip this section for the default disk deployment. To store both attachments and SeaSearch data in S3, set:

ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3
# Leave SS_STORAGE_TYPE empty to follow ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND.
SS_STORAGE_TYPE=
S3_HOST=https://s3-endpoint.example.com
S3_KEY_ID=your-access-key-id
S3_SECRET_KEY=your-secret-access-key
S3_FILE_BUCKET=seaticket-files
S3_WEB_CRAWL_BUCKET=seaticket-connections
S3_SEASEARCH_BUCKET=seaticket-search

Create the buckets needed by the selected backends and grant the credentials read and write access to them. The components using S3 share the following endpoint and credentials:

Variable Description Required when S3_HOST S3-compatible storage endpoint. Attachments or SeaSearch use S3 S3_KEY_ID S3 access key ID. Attachments or SeaSearch use S3 S3_SECRET_KEY S3 secret access key. Attachments or SeaSearch use S3 S3_FILE_BUCKET Bucket for uploaded files. ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 S3_WEB_CRAWL_BUCKET Bucket for connection assets, such as email attachments. ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 S3_SEASEARCH_BUCKET Bucket for SeaSearch data. Compose maps this to S3_SS_BUCKET unless that variable is explicitly set. Resolved SS_STORAGE_TYPE=s3

Advanced S3 options are normally left at their defaults:

Variable Description Default S3_AWS_REGION AWS region used by SeaSearch. us-east-1 S3_USE_V4_SIGNATURE Use Signature Version 4 for SeaSearch S3 requests. true S3_PATH_STYLE_REQUEST Use path-style S3 requests in SeaSearch. true S3_SSE_C_KEY Optional SeaSearch SSE-C encryption key. Requires HTTPS and Signature Version 4. Empty

These advanced options configure SeaSearch. The attachment backend currently uses Signature Version 4 and path-style requests directly; it does not read these four options.

To use different storage backends, set SS_STORAGE_TYPE explicitly. For example, ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=disk with SS_STORAGE_TYPE=s3 keeps attachments on disk and stores SeaSearch data in S3; only the shared S3 credentials, endpoint, and SeaSearch bucket are needed.

docs.title: SeaSearch Settings
docs.text:
Variable Description Default SEASEARCH_URL SeaSearch URL reachable from SeaTicket services. http://seasearch:4080 SEASEARCH_TOKEN Base64 authorization token for the SeaSearch API. Required INIT_SS_ADMIN_USER Optional separate initial SeaSearch account. First team administrator email INIT_SS_ADMIN_PASSWORD Optional separate initial SeaSearch account password. First team administrator password

When both INIT_SS_ADMIN_USER and INIT_SS_ADMIN_PASSWORD are set, SeaSearch uses that separate account. In this case, generate SEASEARCH_TOKEN from those values instead.

docs.title: Optional Extensions
docs.text: The template includes the notification service but does not enable it by default. See Setup Notification Server to enable it.

docs.title: Configure seaticket_config.yaml
docs.text: Configure LLM models and other application settings in /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/conf/seaticket_config.yaml. See SeaTicket YAML Configuration for details.

docs.title: Start SeaTicket
docs.text:
Run Docker Compose from /opt/seaticket:

docker compose up -d

On the first deployment, follow initialization progress:

docker compose logs -f seaqa-web

SeaDB initializes its storage and root account before starting its HTTP service. SeaTicket waits for MySQL/MariaDB and SeaDB, initializes the MySQL database, creates the SeaDB application account, initializes SeaDB template tables, then creates the first team, its administrator, and that administrator's initial workspace. It does not create a system administrator. Sign in with INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_EMAIL and INIT_SEATICKET_TEAM_ADMIN_PASSWORD to use SeaTicket.

After deployment succeeds, remove INIT_SEADB_ROOT_PASSWORD and INIT_SEATICKET_MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD from .env and run docker compose up -d to recreate affected containers. Keep the root passwords backed up for maintenance. Normal restarts use persistent initialization state and application credentials. Keep MySQL application credentials (also used by SeaDB by default), any separate SeaDB credentials, and first-team credentials used as the SeaSearch defaults in .env.

System administrators are optional maintenance accounts. See Account Management when you need to create one.

docs.title: /opt/seadb-data
docs.text: /opt/seadb-data stores SeaDB data and logs.

docs.title: /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data
docs.text:
/opt/seaticket/seaticket-data stores SeaTicket configuration, logs, and persistent application data.

  • conf: SeaTicket configuration files.
  • logs: SeaTicket logs, including seaqa-web.log.
  • seaqa-web-data: Avatar files and custom media.
  • data/attachments: Project and connection attachments when using the disk backend.

docs.title: /opt/seasearch-data
docs.text: The default SS_DATA_PATH stores persistent SeaSearch data. With the disk backend, keep this directory backed up along with the SeaTicket application data.

docs.title: Find Logs
docs.text:
To monitor service logs from the deployment directory:

docker compose logs --follow
docker compose logs --follow seaqa-web

SeaTicket logs are stored under /shared/logs in the container and /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/logs on the host by default.

To monitor all SeaTicket log files on the host:

sudo tail -f $(find /opt/seaticket/seaticket-data/logs/ -type f -name '*.log' 2>/dev/null)
